title: Intervalley coherence and flavor polarization in three-valley moiré systems
authors: Jeyong Park, Laura Classen, Mathias S. Scheurer
abstract: We investigate interaction-induced symmetry breaking in moiré superlattices created by twisting two identical materials where the electronic low-energy degrees of freedom reside in the vicinity of the $M$ points. Based on general symmetry arguments, we identify and classify the possible candidate instabilities that, besides flavor polarized states, also involve a variety of intervalley-coherent (IVC) orders. This complexity is related primarily to the presence of three valleys, instead of the well-studied scenario of two, e.g., in graphene: IVC states can couple all three valleys identically, with a non-trivial sign structure, or even with different magnitudes. We study the energetics using an analytical strong-coupling framework and unrestricted Hartree-Fock applied to the full continuum model, with very good agreement between the two approaches. Interestingly, depending on stacking, IVC instabilities not only appear due to superexchange at moderate bandwidths, but also deep in the strong-coupling regime as a result of deviations from the flat-metric condition. Our work demonstrates that twisted $M$-point materials provide a rich playground for complex correlated physics and highlights differences and similarities to twisted multilayer graphene.
summary: This theoretical work explores emergent electronic orders in three-valley moiré superlattices. By analyzing symmetries and using advanced mean-field techniques, the authors map out a phase diagram showing competition between valley-polarized and intervalley-coherent states. The findings highlight that complex correlated physics, distinct from simpler two-valley systems like graphene, dictates the ground state depending on stacking geometry and interaction strength.
main_problem: The study investigates interaction-induced symmetry breaking and determines the energetically favored ground state orders (IVC vs. flavor-polarized) in moiré superlattices possessing three electronic valleys.
main_result: The system exhibits a rich variety of intervalley-coherent (IVC) phases, which can be stabilized either by superexchange at moderate bandwidths or deep within the strong-coupling regime due to deviations from flat-metric conditions.
method: The analysis combines symmetry arguments with advanced theoretical techniques, including unrestricted Hartree-Fock calculations and analytical strong-coupling frameworks applied to a continuum model.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as moiré superlattices formed by twisting two identical materials whose low-energy physics resides near the M points, featuring three distinct valleys ($\eta=1, 2, 3$). The Hamiltonian incorporates both single-particle dispersion and repulsive density-density interactions.
key_observables: Valley Polarization (VP) order parameters, Intervalley Coherent Order parameters ($	ext{IVC}_{3\pm}$, NIVC), and the resulting band structure gaps/insulating nature.
important_parameters:
Twist angle ($	heta$), interaction strength parameterized by relative permittivity ($\epsilon_r$), and electron filling fraction ($

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field decoupling (Hartree-Fock) and often assumes the strong-coupling limit or uses perturbation theory to treat deviations from ideal conditions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate moiré band structures, phase diagrams mapping ground state character ($	ext{VP}$, $	ext{IVC}$ phases) against parameters like $	heta$ and $\epsilon_r$, and order parameter dependencies on these tuning knobs.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the symmetry constraints of the three-valley system, then applying strong-coupling/Hartree-Fock methods to map out candidate ordered states ($	ext{IVC}$ vs. $	ext{VP}$), and finally using perturbation theory to determine which state minimizes the total energy under varying physical conditions.
why_interesting: The detailed symmetry analysis and classification of correlated phases in a multi-valley system provide a template for understanding complex electronic ordering driven by geometry, relevant to topological materials and strongly interacting quantum systems.
